name: Battle of Vercellae
intro: The Raudine Plain in northern Italy, at the end of July. You are Gaius Marius, consul for the fifth time, with your colleague Catulus: about 52,000 men in all. The Cimbri under Boiorix have crossed the Alps, perhaps 120,000 warriors or more with their families and wagons.
debrief: In reality, the Cimbri asked for land for themselves and the Teutones; Marius said the Teutones already had land, given by Rome, and showed the envoys their captive kings. Boiorix offered battle and let the Romans choose the place. The Romans formed facing west, so that the morning sun and the wind-blown dust were in the Cimbri’s faces. The Cimbri horse swung away in what may have been a feint; Sulla’s cavalry then drove it back into the Cimbri infantry. Catulus’s centre advanced with pila and swords, the wings closed in, and the Cimbri, suffering in the heat, were driven back onto their wagons; Boiorix died fighting. The site is disputed (traditionally near Vercelli; some argue for the Po delta). Roman losses are put at a few hundred to a thousand, and Cimbri losses at 65,000 to well over 100,000. Marius and Catulus later quarrelled over the credit. The other choices are what-ifs.

win: The Cimbri are driven onto their wagons.
lose: Italy lies open to the north.

options.text: Envoys shaken, you choose the ground
Sun and wind at your back

decisions.title: The envoys
decisions.text: Cimbri envoys come to your camp. They demand land for themselves and for their kin, the Teutones.

hint.text: The Teutones were destroyed at Aquae Sextiae last year. Their kings are your prisoners.

scout.text: Showing the envoys their captured kings will shake the Cimbri and make their king hurry to fight on your terms.

choices.label: Show them their captured kings in chains

fx.text: Marius says the Teutones already have land, given them by Rome. Then he shows the envoys their kings in chains. Boiorix offers battle and lets you choose the place and day.

choices.label: Offer them poor land in the north to buy time

fx.text: The Senate will never agree. The Cimbri take it as weakness.

choices.label: Send them away without an answer and make them wait

fx.text: The Cimbri stay where they are and wait.

decisions.title: Choosing the battlefield
decisions.text: Boiorix leaves the choice of ground to you. It is high summer. The Cimbri come from the north and have never fought in Italian heat.

hint.text: The Raudine Plain is dry and dusty. The sun will rise behind you if you face west.

scout.text: Face west on the open plain: the morning sun is in their eyes and the wind carries your dust into their faces. Form first and let them come.

choices.label: The open plain, sun and wind at your back

fx.text: The army forms early, facing west. The morning sun flashes on your helmets and the wind blows your dust into the Cimbri’s faces.
You form on the plain, but the Cimbri have chosen their own hour.

choices.label: The hills, where their cavalry cannot ride

fx.text: The hills slow the Cimbri horse, but they also break up your line.

choices.label: Let them choose, and learn where they mean to fight

fx.text: The Cimbri choose ground that suits them.

decisions.title: The horsemen turn
decisions.text: The Cimbri come on in a huge square, their 15,000 horsemen in front. Suddenly the horsemen swing to your right, as if to retreat or to ride round.

hint.text: Some of your legionaries are starting to run after them.

scout.text: A feigned retreat is the oldest trick there is. Men who chase it lose their formation and are cut down by the next wave.

choices.label: Hold the line; let no one pursue

fx.text: The officers hold the ranks. The Cimbri, dazzled by the sun, cannot tell where your line is weak.

choices.label: Send the legions after the horse while it flees

fx.text: The pursuers break ranks and the Cimbri infantry falls on them.

choices.label: Wheel the right wing to face them

fx.text: The wing turns, but a gap opens beside it.

decisions.title: Sulla’s cavalry
decisions.text: On the far right, your cavalry under Lucius Cornelius Sulla faces the Cimbri horse as it swings round.

hint.text: The Cimbri horsemen are bunched up after their turn.

scout.text: Cavalry that hits bunched horsemen from the flank can drive them back into their own infantry.

fx.text: Sulla’s horse crashes into the Cimbri cavalry and drives it back into its own infantry. The great square is thrown into chaos.

choices.label: Send the cavalry to burn the wagons and their families’ supplies

fx.text: Sulla’s horse is far from the fight.

decisions.title: Heat and iron
decisions.text: The Cimbri infantry is in disorder and suffering in the heat. Catulus’s centre faces the mass of them.

hint.text: The Cimbri are tiring in the heat.

scout.text: Pila first, then swords at close quarters. Let the wings close on both flanks, and drive them back onto their own wagons.

choices.label: Advance the centre and close both wings

fx.text: The pila fall, the swords come out, and the wings close in. The Cimbri are driven back against their wagons. Boiorix and his nobles die fighting.
The Cimbri are driven back toward their wagons.

choices.label: Charge the whole army straight ahead

fx.text: The charge hits the mass head-on.

choices.label: Hold back; the heat is already beating them for you
